section: Educational Psychology · Ch — Special Needs & Inclusive Education
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A model in which children with disabilities attend regular mainstream schools alongside non-disabled peers, but are expected to adapt to the existing curriculum and structure with only limited additional support (e.g., attending a resource room for part of the day), is called:
explanation: Integrated Education places disabled children in mainstream schools but the CHILD must adapt to the existing system — unlike Inclusive Education, which restructures the school's curriculum, teaching methods, and environment to accommodate all learners' diverse needs, placing the onus of adaptation on the SYSTEM rather than the child.
